title: Tensor comparison from elementwise directed algebra presentations
statement:
Let $R\to T$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $J$ be a small nonempty directed preorder. Let $(A_i,a_{ij})$ be a directed diagram of commutative $R$-algebras and $(B_i,b_{ij})$ a directed diagram of commutative $T$-algebras, for $i\le j$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Let $C$ be a commutative $R$-algebra and $D$ a commutative $T$-algebra, with compatible algebra cocone maps $\rho_i:A_i\to C$ and $\sigma_i:B_i\to D$. Suppose every element of $C$ lies in some $\rho_i(A_i)$, and whenever $\rho_i(x)=\rho_i(y)$ there is $j\ge i$ with $a_{ij}(x)=a_{ij}(y)$. Impose the corresponding two conditions on $D$, $\sigma_i$ and $b_{ij}$. Regard all $T$-algebras as $R$-algebras through $R\to T$. Suppose $p:C\to D$ and $p_i:A_i\to B_i$ are $R$-algebra maps satisfying $p\rho_i=\sigma_i p_i$ and $b_{ij}p_i=p_j a_{ij}$. Suppose the canonical $T$-algebra maps
$$\varphi_i:A_i\otimes_RT\longrightarrow B_i,\qquad x\otimes t\longmapsto p_i(x)t$$
are isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Then $(C,\rho_i)$ and $(D,\sigma_i)$ are colimit cocones of the underlying $R$-module diagrams [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; $(C\otimes_RT,\rho_i\otimes1)$ is a colimit cocone for the underlying $R$-module diagram $(A_i\otimes_RT,a_{ij}\otimes1)$. There is a unique $R$-linear isomorphism $\Phi:C\otimes_RT\to D$ satisfying
$$\Phi\circ(\rho_i\otimes1)=\sigma_i\circ\varphi_i.$$
This $\Phi$ is the canonical $T$-algebra isomorphism characterized by
$$\Phi(c\otimes t)=p(c)t\qquad(c\in C,\ t\in T).$$
All tensor products here are algebra tensor products, with scalar structure through the right-hand factor $T$ [def-weil-module-base-change].

proof.text: Reduce the two module colimit assertions to the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion]. The small nonempty directed preorder $J$, viewed as a category with one arrow $i\to j$ for each $i\le j$, is a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: it is nonempty, two objects have a common upper bound, and parallel arrows are equal. Every $a_{ij}$ and every $\rho_i$ is an $R$-algebra map, hence $R$-linear; every $b_{ij}$ and every $\sigma_i$ is a $T$-algebra map, hence $R$-linear for the $R$-module structures through $R\to T$. So $(A_i,a_{ij})$ and $(B_i,b_{ij})$ are diagrams of $R$-modules and $(C,\rho_i)$, $(D,\sigma_i)$ are cocones on them. The exhaustion hypotheses are clause (1) of that node, and the same-stage eventual-equality hypotheses (if $\rho_i(x)=\rho_i(y)$, then $a_{ij}(x)=a_{ij}(y)$ for some $j\ge i$; likewise for $\sigma_i$, $b_{ij}$) are its clause (2), with $f$ the arrow $i\to j$. No transition map is assumed injective.

source.place: Tag 00D6, lemma-directed-colimit: representative relation; the converse criterion here is checked directly from the hypotheses

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] to the cocone $(C,\rho_i)$ on $(A_i,a_{ij})$ and to the cocone $(D,\sigma_i)$ on $(B_i,b_{ij})$, both in $R$-modules, with the hypotheses checked in step 1. It gives that both are colimit cocones of the underlying $R$-module diagrams in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: for every compatible family of $R$-linear maps $f_i:A_i\to M$ (resp. $B_i\to M$) there is exactly one $R$-linear map $f$ from $C$ (resp. $D$) with $f\rho_i=f_i$ (resp. $f\sigma_i=f_i$). These are the first two asserted module colimits and the universal properties used in steps 4 and 5.

source.place: Tag 00D6, lemma-directed-colimit; Tag 00DA, lemma-homomorphism-limit (the elementwise description of a directed colimit of modules)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits] to the module colimit $(C,\rho_i)$ from step 2 and the fixed $R$-module $T$. Since $J$ is small, this gives a colimit with vertex $C\otimes_RT$ and legs $\lambda_i=\rho_i\otimes1$ for the diagram with transition maps $\alpha_{ij}=a_{ij}\otimes1$. These are the underlying linear maps of the algebra tensor maps: on pure tensors both send $x\otimes t$ to $\rho_i(x)\otimes t$ or $a_{ij}(x)\otimes t$, respectively [def-weil-module-base-change].

The stage maps form a compatible isomorphism of module diagrams: on $x\otimes t$, $b_{ij}\varphi_i(x\otimes t)=b_{ij}(p_i(x)t)=p_j(a_{ij}(x))t=\varphi_j\alpha_{ij}(x\otimes t)$ because $b_{ij}$ is a $T$-algebra map. Equality extends by the defining linearity of the tensor product. Therefore $\varphi_j\alpha_{ij}=b_{ij}\varphi_i$, and composing with inverses gives $\varphi_j^{-1}b_{ij}=\alpha_{ij}\varphi_i^{-1}$. The colimit properties [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of steps 2 and 3 now give unique $R$-linear maps $\Phi:C\otimes_RT\to D$ and $\Psi:D\to C\otimes_RT$ with $\Phi\lambda_i=\sigma_i\varphi_i$ and $\Psi\sigma_i=\lambda_i\varphi_i^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 00DA, lemma-homomorphism-limit: induced map; inverse compatibility written explicitly

proof.text: For each $i$, $\Psi\Phi\lambda_i=\Psi\sigma_i\varphi_i=\lambda_i\varphi_i^{-1}\varphi_i=\lambda_i$, while $\Phi\Psi\sigma_i=\Phi\lambda_i\varphi_i^{-1}=\sigma_i$. The uniqueness clause of the two colimit universal properties [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] implies $\Psi\Phi=1$ and $\Phi\Psi=1$. Thus $\Phi$ is an $R$-linear isomorphism, and the same uniqueness clause gives the required uniqueness among maps satisfying its displayed compatibility.

source.place: Tag 00DA, lemma-homomorphism-limit; two inverse identities verified on the cocone legs

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], clause (2), to $p:C\to D$ and the structure map $T\to D$. It gives an $R$-algebra map $h:C\otimes_RT\to D$ with $h(c\otimes t)=p(c)t$. On pure tensors $h\lambda_i(x\otimes t)=p(\rho_i(x))t=\sigma_i(p_i(x))t=\sigma_i\varphi_i(x\otimes t)$, since $\sigma_i$ is a $T$-algebra map. Hence $h=\Phi$ by the module colimit uniqueness. Moreover $h(1\otimes t)=t$, so it is a $T$-algebra map for the right-factor scalar structure [def-weil-module-base-change]. For $d,e\in D$ and $t\in T$, the identities $h(\Psi(d)\Psi(e))=de=h(\Psi(de))$, $h(1)=1=h(\Psi(1))$, and $h(t\Psi(d))=td=h(\Psi(td))$ imply, by injectivity of $h$, that $\Psi$ preserves products, unit and $T$-scalars. It is already additive by step 4. Thus this same $\Phi$ is the claimed canonical $T$-algebra isomorphism with the stated formula.
